svg.title: One file changed deep in a directory: the trees above it renamed, one by one up to the top
svg.text: the trees and blobs, as ls-tree -r -t lists them

g.title: After add and write-tree: one tree for each directory, built bottom up, and the top one, dcd4984, stands for all five files. The index keeps each directory's tree.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
tree: / (4 entries, 5 files under it): dcd4984, built

g.title: d/e/f.txt gets a line, and add stores it: new bytes, so a new blob, 06654ae, and the file's index entry names it now.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;

g.title: The same add forgets the cached tree of every directory above d/e/f.txt: the top, d and d/e. b keeps its own, since nothing under it changed.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
index: d/e/f.txt changed: the cached tree of / is gone
index: d/e/f.txt changed: the cached tree of d/ is gone
index: d/e/f.txt changed: the cached tree of d/e/ is gone

g.title: write-tree, bottom up. b's cached tree is still good, so 1933da3 is taken as it is: no tree is built for b.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
tree: b/ (1 file under it): 1933da3, from the cache

g.title: d/e built. Its one entry, f.txt, names 06654ae now: its bytes changed, so its name did, 8588183 becomes cd21a79.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
tree: d/e/ (1 entry, 1 file under it): cd21a79, built

g.title: d built. It lists e by e's new name, and g.txt as before: its bytes changed, so its name did, d61f885 becomes 7ecc4e4.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
tree: d/ (2 entries, 2 files under it): 7ecc4e4, built

g.title: The top built. It lists d by d's new name, and b c, b and hello.txt as before: its bytes changed, so its name did, dcd4984 becomes 6f0dd63. Three trees built, one from the cache: every tree on the path to f.txt has a new name, and nothing else does.
g.text: each directory's last tree, with how
many index entries are under it;
tree: / (4 entries, 5 files under it): 6f0dd63, built
